key_provisions_or_claims: A robot can be legally classified as a product, so producers or suppliers are liable for defect, damage and causation.
Traditional liability rules are inadequate given AI autonomy, complexity and multiple parties.
Victims may still claim under liability for things (guardianship) alongside defective-product liability.
Contractual exemption, limitation or aggravation of liability is limited, e.g. invalid for fraud or gross fault.
Recommends specific AI liability legislation, risk-based liability for high-risk applications and compulsory insurance.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed Arabic article analysing civil liability for harm caused by AI and robots under Iraqi and French law. It argues robots can be treated as products under defective-product liability but traditional rules are inadequate, and recommends specific legislation, risk-based liability for high-risk uses and compulsory insurance.
